gen_risks.description: Construction of the new Citizen Service Center facility in Tirana could generate localized environmental impacts such as dust, noise, waste generation, traffic disruption, and safety hazards.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate the site-specific Environmental Management Plan (EMP) into bidding documents and construction contracts, ensure supervisor monitoring, and comply with Albanian construction permitting laws.
gen_risks.evidence: Operational policy OP 4.01 is triggered and the project categorized as a World Bank Category B because a new building will be constructed for CSC

gen_risks.description: ADISA is a newly established agency with limited implementation track record and weak procurement/fiduciary capacity, risking project execution delays and non-compliance with World Bank guidelines.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a dedicated PMU within ADISA staffed with qualified procurement and FM specialists, provide continuous World Bank fiduciary training, and utilize MoF's CFCU during the PPF phase.
gen_risks.evidence: Created in October 2014, ADISA has a limited track record of implementation experience, but some members of the project team have relevant experience.

gen_risks.description: Civil servants and participating line agencies may resist ceding front-office service delivery to ADISA/CSCs, potentially undermining business process re-engineering and service integration.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement a structured change management and outreach program, engage agency reform champions, and establish clear communications to align civil service incentives with new service standards.
gen_risks.evidence: Ministries, agencies and individual civil servants may not welcome ceding the front office function to CSC. Bureaucratic resistance could stifle efforts to improve back-office functions.

gen_risks.description: Heavy emphasis on online service delivery and high-end urban Citizen Service Centers risks excluding poor, rural, elderly, and marginalized populations with low digital literacy or access.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain alternative physical access points, establish assisted digital access network points (e.g., at local government centers and internet cafes), offer call center helplines, and conduct targeted outreach.
gen_risks.evidence: there is a risk that the focus on state-of-the-art means for service delivery, such as online services or high-end urban CSCs, will diminish access

gen_risks.description: High operational complexity and inter-sectoral coordination requirements across more than ten participating ministries and agencies could cause decision-making bottlenecks and implementation delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain strong oversight through the Prime Minister-led Inter-Ministerial Public Services Committee, Technical Inter-Ministerial Committee, and active progress monitoring and barrier-unblocking by the Delivery Unit.
gen_risks.evidence: Inter-sectoral reforms, especially those that involve more than a dozen government agencies, necessarily entail complex coordination.

gen_risks.description: An ambitious and compressed reform timeline for process re-engineering, legislative updates, and service automation may result in missed target dates and delayed disbursements under the results-based loan.
gen_risks.mitigation: Balance quick-win interventions with long-term structural reforms, structure results-based financing across a 5-year timeline, and provide just-in-time technical assistance to participating agencies.
gen_risks.evidence: The Government’s timeline for the reform is very ambitious.

gen_risks.description: Manual payroll processes and unintegrated accounting systems across participating budgetary and non-budgetary agencies create financial management control risks in Eligible Expenditure Programs (EEPs).
gen_risks.mitigation: Adopt a comprehensive Financial Management Manual, recruit qualified PMU finance specialists, procure dedicated project accounting software, and conduct annual High State Control audits of EEPs.
gen_risks.evidence: The overall financial management risk is rated as Substantial.

gen_risks.description: Incomplete digitization, missing National ID records, and unresolved legal ownership issues in legacy state databases (e.g., IPRO) could hinder backend system integration and automation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide targeted technical assistance and financing to digitize legacy paper records, clean up data, link National IDs, and integrate agency databases with NAIS's government interoperability platform.
gen_risks.evidence: The National ID number is missing for most records, only 45 to 50 percent of the archive is digitized, and legal issues over ownership remain

gen_risks.description: Discrepancies between official internal administrative processing logs and actual citizen transaction times could result in inaccurate baseline assessment and unreliable performance monitoring.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize independent bi-annual user surveys, deploy third-party validation (TPV) for DLI achievements, and implement proactive SMS citizen feedback mechanisms to capture real user experience.
gen_risks.evidence: This anomaly could be the result of poor reporting of data or poor definition of the process.

gen_risks.description: Delays in drafting and parliamentary approval of mandatory omnibus primary legislation and secondary bylaws could halt the legal enactment of re-engineered business processes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Mobilize ministerial working groups overseen by the Technical Inter-Ministerial Committee to prepare legal inventories early and engage legal consultants under TA to draft the omnibus bill.
gen_risks.evidence: Reform of government services and repeal of licenses, permits, and approvals will be implemented through omnibus legislation, expected to be passed by the end of 2016.

gen_risks.description: Inadequate long-term budget allocations for ongoing ICT software licensing, hardware maintenance, and periodic upgrades could compromise the operational sustainability of digitized services.
gen_risks.mitigation: Detail full lifecycle recurrent cost requirements in the approved Reform Policy Document, secure explicit government budget commitments, and explore public-private partnership (PPP) operational models.
gen_risks.evidence: Ongoing operating costs are expected to include licenses and system operation and maintenance. To continue efficiency improvements once services have been automated, the Government will have to upgrade periodically.

gen_risks.description: Strong dependence on top-level political leadership creates vulnerability if cabinet turnover or shifting political priorities erode institutional support for service delivery reforms.
gen_risks.mitigation: Institutionalize reform mandates within permanent structures (ADISA, NAIS, Delivery Unit), anchor financial support to five-year DLIs, and generate public demand via open citizen feedback reporting.
gen_risks.evidence: There is high level political commitment and push, which is a great asset to the project. The compressed implementation timeline is a potential risk

gt_risks.description: Institutional capacity poses challenges to delivering the reform effort, despite very high leadership commitment and fast-paced GoA initiation of reforms.
gt_risks.mitigation: The Project Preparation Facility (PPF) is designed to assist capacity building for the implementing agency; the TA part of the loan continues building capacity to deliver, addressing the most pressing capacity needs.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risks related to the new form of financial instrument used in Albania.
gt_risks.mitigation: The TA part of the loan helps mitigate the fiduciary risk by supporting fiduciary and budget specialists in the PMU.

gt_risks.description: Technical design risk, named alongside the fiduciary risk as being addressed by the same TA support (fiduciary and budget specialists in the PMU); not separately elaborated beyond this.
gt_risks.mitigation: The TA part of the loan helps mitigate the technical design risk by supporting fiduciary and budget specialists in the PMU.

gt_risks.description: Stakeholder risks arising from inter-agency coordination.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigated by strong emphasis on coordination mechanisms in the design of the operation.

gt_risks.description: Bureaucratic resistance to enhanced transparency and simplification of administrative processes.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigated in part through high-level leadership and engagement, and through citizen feedback arrangements that help pinpoint poor performance and corruption.

gt_risks.description: Political cycle risk from elections coming up in 2017, which could disrupt reform continuity and government commitment.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigated by making early progress in showing results and ensuring a broad constituency of support for the project's objectives and activities among the leadership of participating institutions and service users.
